The code changes introduce a potential issue in the `writeTo` method of the `MvExpand` class where an assertion is made that `limit` must be `null`. This assertion conflicts with test cases that expect non-null limits to be properly handled and serialized.
The assertion in `MvExpand.java`:
```java
assert limit == null;
```
This assertion will fail when the `limit` is non-null, as required by several test cases (e.g., `testSortMvExpandLimit`, `testWhereMvExpand`). The assertion appears to be a placeholder or an oversight, as it directly contradicts the intended functionality demonstrated in the tests.
### Suggested Changes:
1. Remove the assertion in the `writeTo` method to allow non-null limits to be serialized correctly.
2. Ensure that the `writeTo` method properly handles the `limit` field when it is non-null.
This issue could cause runtime assertion failures and test failures if the code is executed with non-null limits, as expected by the test cases.

review_comment: Perhaps a comment here might be a good idea. The PR description explains this very nicely, but I imagine someone reading this code later might be a little confused.

review_comment: Interesting that this code previously did not push the limit down past the MvExpand at all, but the bug reports indicate that that was happening. Was it happening somewhere else? If so, should that location be modified?

Oh yeah, good point, I forgot about it...
We have another rule, called `DuplicateLimitAfterMvExpand`, that does exactly what I describe above: 
`MV_EXPAND | LIMIT` -> `LIMIT | MV_EXPAND | LIMIT`

I think we can remove it

There is another rule, [AddDefaultTopN](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/optimizer/rules/logical/AddDefaultTopN.java), that is intrinsically wrong (it adds an arbitrary limit at the beginning of the query) and that IMHO should be removed as well, but I'm not sure this fix is enough to do it, maybe the problems it tries to solve are not only related to MV_EXPAND.
